instructions: Transfer the tuna to a fine sieve over the sink. Press down with the back of a spoon until it stops dripping, then transfer it to a large bowl and flake it with a fork.
Trim the lemongrass and peel off the tough outer layers. Slice the bottom 4 inches very thin, then chop it fine. That should be about 2 tbsp.
Thinly slice the shallots and the green onions. Pick the leaves from half the cilantro bunch and half the mint bunch, and tear the mint into small pieces.
Juice the 2 limes into a small bowl. That should be about 1/4 cup. Stir in the 2 tbsp fish sauce and the 1 1/2 tsp sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the dressing over the tuna. Add the shallots, lemongrass and green onions and toss.
Add the cilantro and mint and toss lightly. Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash more fish sauce.
Pull the lettuce leaves apart and slice the cucumber.
Spoon the tuna salad into the lettuce leaves and serve with the cucumber slices. Put the red pepper flakes on the table for anyone who wants heat.
To pack it for lunch, keep the tuna salad in a covered container in the fridge for up to 2 days and pack the lettuce and cucumber separately. Don't freeze it.
method_notes: Hungry in Thailand, Marion's Kitchen and Riverside Thai Cooking all dress drained canned tuna with fish sauce, lime and a little sugar, then add shallot and herbs. Hungry in Thailand adds lemongrass and Marion's adds mint with lettuce and cucumber to serve; Marion's uses a stronger dressing, so this one sits between the two. The chili is left on the side as pepper flakes so the base stays mild. Every page has only 1 rating, so the lead is a fallback.
